# Blog post: persistent memory for coding agents over MCP, a case study

## Context

This is the week's post under the November operating page (private, business #19): one or two posts a week, each publish request naming its search term, title, cover, target reader and the strongest reason that reader would skip it, all before the operator's click. Area G's term for this week, chosen against #20184's grid audience: **`ai agent persistent memory mcp`**, with `mcp memory server`, `coding agent persistent memory` and `context compaction recovery` as secondary terms. The publish request is due Thu Nov 5.

## The Problem

A coding agent loses its working context between sessions and at every context compaction. It re-reads the codebase, re-derives decisions and can repeat a fix that was rejected two sessions ago. Builders who hit this search the term above and mostly find thin wrappers that push a vector store's top hits into the prompt. We run a system that solves this for a team of AI maintainers every day, and no post explains it.

## The Architectural Reality: what the post may claim, each with its receipt

- **A loaded index plus a pulled archive.** The repository's rules and each seat's short, self-curated memory index load every session. The archive is pulled over MCP with three separate tools, and nothing from it enters a prompt unasked:
  - `query_recent_turns`, the chronological feed, summary-first;
  - `query_raw_memories`, semantic recall;
  - `add_memory`, the end-of-turn consolidation an agent writes deliberately.
  The agent decides what to pull.
- **Scale, measured 2026-11-03 06:11Z:** 55,022 turns in 5,332 sessions in the shared store. Embeddings run on a local model (`qwen3-embedding-8b`) and session summaries on a local `gemma-4-26b`, so the memory stays on the machine. Every number is re-measured on the publish day.
- **What an outsider can do today.** `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` is public, but there is no npm package and no registry install for the memory server: of its six `server.json` manifests, only `neural-link` declares a package. Running it means a clone and a self-hosted plane, following the deployment guides. (#20114's one-command onboarding excludes the Memory Core, so it is not this server's install path.)

Design authority: n/a. The ticket is new content and calls no existing behavior wrong.

## The Fix

`learn/blog/<slug>.md`, registered in `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json`, written to `/blog-post`:
- a thesis-first arc: the reader's problem; why prompt-stuffing vector memory falls short; pull-only recency, recall and consolidation; why it holds by construction;
- receipts from our own trail, including a compaction recovery;
- honest bounds;
- a candid CTA: read the code, and run it from a clone with its rough edges named.

The title passes the stranger worst-parse test and the five over-claim checks, and carries no number without a dated receipt.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The post and its `blog.json` registration land, render-verified at `#/news/blog/<id>`.
- [ ] AC-2: Every number is measured and dated, and every external claim is sourced and linked.
- [ ] AC-3: The CTA claims no one-command install of the memory server.
- [ ] AC-4: Area G's hardest read plus at least one more model review, from a different family than the author; the operator approves last.
- [ ] AC-5 (post-merge): the publish request on business #19 carries the term, title, cover, target reader and skip reason.

## Out of Scope

A one-command install of the memory server, and its cold-run proof; a video.
